subtitle: At Takkolam, a prince falls, an empire buckles, and a single arrow divides memory

panels.shot: wide, storm-dark battlefield tableau framing two distant war elephants facing each other, one bearing Rajaditya, the other symbolising Krishna III’s advancing might
panels.action: Rajaditya stands tall upon his armoured elephant in the smoky dusk of Takkolam as distant Rashtrakuta banners close in, the air thick with dust, spears, and the tense stillness before impact.

dialogue.text: At Takkolam, a Chola prince dies on an elephant, a Rashtrakuta king wins a realm — and the stone records still argue over whose arrow toppled him.

i18n.hi: तक्कोलम में, एक चोल राजकुमार हाथी पर मरा, एक राष्ट्रकूट राजा ने राज जीता — और पत्थर आज भी बहस करते हैं किसके तीर ने उसे गिराया।

panels.shot: slow aerial drift over a map-like Deccan and Tamil country, rivers and hill ranges faintly traced beneath clouds
panels.action: An imagined map of peninsular India lies under passing clouds, the Kaveri delta, Deccan plateau and Eastern Ghats faintly lit as if by flickering torches along ancient routes.

dialogue.text: Mid–10th century. From the Kaveri to the Krishna, two powers strain against each other: the rising Cholas of Parantaka I and the Rashtrakutas of Krishna III.

i18n.hi: दसवीं सदी के बीच का समय। कावेरी से कृष्णा तक, दो ताकतें भिड़ी हैं: परांतक-पहले के उभरते चोल और कृष्ण-तीसरे के राष्ट्रकूट।

panels.shot: split composition, left showing Parantaka’s court, right showing early Krishna III in Deccan, both in three-quarter medium shots
panels.action: On one side, a regal Chola court with Parantaka I seated while a younger Rajaditya stands near; on the other, an austere Deccan hall where Krishna III, still lean and watchful, listens to his generals.

dialogue.text: Parantaka’s banners have gone north, past Kanchi. Krishna III has already crushed rivals on the Deccan. Between them lies the road through Tondai Nadu.

i18n.hi: परांतक के झंडे कांची पार उत्तर तक जा चुके हैं। कृष्ण तीसरा दक्कन के दुश्मनों को कुचल चुका है। बीच में है तोंडै नाडु की राह।

panels.shot: medium shot on Rajaditya in armor beside a temple gopuram, low angle to emphasize his youth and resolve
panels.action: Rajaditya, broad-shouldered and youthful, adjusts his lamellar armour near a Chola temple, his elephant waiting behind as priests and officers watch with mixed pride and apprehension.

dialogue.speaker: Rajaditya
dialogue.text: Father took the north once. I will hold it.

i18n.hi: पिता ने उत्तर जीता था। मैं उसे संभालूँगा।

panels.shot: close-up on Krishna III’s face in profile as he studies a palm-leaf map by lamplight
panels.action: Krishna III leans over a palm-leaf map marked with small metal tokens, his face lit by a single oil lamp as Western Ganga allies stand respectfully in shadow behind him.

dialogue.text: To Krishna III, the Chola advance is not distant news. It is a challenge. He draws in allies like the Western Ganga prince Butuga, and plans to break the southern thrust at its tip.

i18n.hi: कृष्ण तीसरे के लिए चोलों की बढ़त दूर की खबर नहीं, चुनौती है। वह पश्चिमी गंग राजकुमार बुतुगा जैसे साथियों को जोड़ता है, और दक्षिण की धार वहीं तोड़ने की सोचता है।

panels.shot: broad battlefield establishing shot of Takkolam plain with two approaching armies under a washed-out sun
panels.action: On the dry plains near Takkolam, two armies spread like dark stains across the land, Chola standards of the tiger facing Rashtrakuta and Ganga emblems, dust plumes rising as elephants and cavalry step into range.

dialogue.text: The clash comes at Takkolam in the North Arcot region, around 948 or 949. Later inscriptions will remember this ground with more certainty than many of the men who marched onto it.

i18n.hi: टक्कर होती है तक्कोलम में, नॉर्थ आर्कोट इलाके में, करीब 948–949 में। बाद की शिलालेख इस मिट्टी को उन सिपाहियों से ज़्यादा साफ याद रखेंगे जो यहाँ चले थे।

panels.shot: dynamic medium-wide of Rajaditya on his elephant in the front line, viewed from the level of marching infantry
panels.action: Rajaditya stands upright in his howdah, hand on a spear, as his war elephant lumbers forward at the Chola front, soldiers below glancing up to him as their anchor in the chaos.

dialogue.text: Both Chola and later Chola-side copper plates agree on one stark image: Rajaditya, the prince, fighting from the back of an elephant at Takkolam.

i18n.hi: चोल और बाद के चोल-पक्ष के ताम्रपट एक ही सख्त तस्वीर दोहराते हैं: राजादित्य, राजकुमार, तakkोलम में हाथी की पीठ से लड़ता हुआ।

panels.shot: low-angle shot from behind Rashtrakuta-Ganga ranks as they sight the Chola elephant line in the distance
panels.action: Through a forest of spears and bows, the silhouette of Rajaditya’s elephant looms ahead, while allied commanders point and shout orders amid the tightening ranks of Rashtrakuta and Ganga warriors.

dialogue.text: From the Rashtrakuta side, a near-contemporary stone at Atakur, in Kannada, will later carve a different detail: that Western Ganga prince Butuga brings down this elephant-borne foe.

i18n.hi: राष्ट्रकूट तरफ से, आतकूर की पास की एक लगभग समकालीन कन्नड़ शिला और बात कहती है: पश्चिमी गंग राजकुमार बुतुगा यही हाथी-सवार दुश्मन गिराता है।

panels.shot: intense mid-shot of archers and spearmen in the melee, arrows frozen mid-flight in the sky
panels.action: Arrows arc through the hazy sky, spearmen surge forward, and the line between both hosts compresses into a desperate push, Rajaditya’s elephant partly obscured by dust and the press of men.

dialogue.text: No eyewitness account survives to walk us blow by blow through Takkolam. Only stone and copper, terse and proud, speak from both sides centuries later.

i18n.hi: कोई आँखों–देखी कहानी नहीं बची जो हमें तakkोलम की हर चोट दिखाए। बस पत्थर और ताम्र, कम शब्द, ऊँचा गर्व, सदियों बाद दोनों तरफ से बोलते हैं।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot on Rajaditya atop the elephant, head turned sharply as if reacting to something unseen
panels.action: Rajaditya turns suddenly atop his elephant, eyes wide, as if feeling the battle tilt; the beast’s trunk curls, its tusks capped in metal, while panicked retainers cling to the howdah rails.

dialogue.speaker: Rajaditya
dialogue.text: Hold the line. We must not break.

i18n.hi: पंक्ति मत टूटने दो। हमें नहीं टूटना है।

panels.shot: tight, slightly low-angle shot of Krishna III on horseback or chariot, gesturing forward amidst his guards
panels.action: Krishna III, armoured and composed, rides forward with his guard, one hand raised in a cutting gesture toward the Chola centre as his standard-bearer keeps the imperial emblem aloft.

dialogue.text: What we do know is the outcome that both traditions accept: under Krishna III’s leadership, the Rashtrakuta alliance shatters the Chola army, and the prince on the elephant does not leave this field alive.

i18n.hi: जो तय है, वह अंजाम है जिसे दोनों परंपराएँ मानती हैं: कृष्ण तीसरे की अगुवाई में राष्ट्रकूट गठजोड़ चोल सेना को तोड़ देता है, और हाथी पर बैठा राजकुमार ज़िंदा मैदान नहीं छोड़ता।

panels.shot: suspended wide shot of the Chola elephant beginning to tilt in the melee, without showing explicit impact
panels.action: In the swirl of combat, Rajaditya’s elephant lurches, its massive body beginning to tilt as soldiers below reach up in alarm, the entire frame capturing a single breath of imbalance.

dialogue.text: Later lore will picture a single deadly shaft. The record, more cautious, only agrees that on that beast, in that battle, Rajaditya falls and the Chola line collapses around him.

i18n.hi: बाद की कथा इसे एक ही घातक बाण में समेटती है। अभिलेख, ज़्यादा सँभलकर, बस मानते हैं कि उसी हाथी पर, उसी लड़ाई में, राजादित्य गिरा और चोल पंक्ति उसके चारों तरफ ढह गई।

panels.shot: somber mid-shot aftermath of the battlefield, with discarded weapons and distant smoke, no bodies foregrounded
panels.action: The battlefield lies quiet under a dull sky, spears stuck in the earth, a broken Chola tiger banner drooping while distant columns of Rashtrakuta troops move across the haze like dark threads.

dialogue.text: For the Cholas, this is no minor setback. Takkolam halts their northern surge. Their king Parantaka outlives his son; his empire, for a time, shrinks under the weight of defeat.

i18n.hi: चोलों के लिए यह मामूली झटका नहीं। तakkोलम उनकी उत्तरी लहर रोक देता है। उनका राजा परांतक बेटे से ज़्यादा जीता है; उसका राज, कुछ समय को, हार के बोझ से सिमट जाता है।

panels.shot: close-up on a sculptor carving Kannada letters into stone, hands steady, chisel striking sparks
panels.action: A stonecutter under a shade tree leans over a slab, chisel in hand, carefully carving flowing Kannada script as a patron in Rashtrakuta-style attire watches with satisfaction.

dialogue.text: Near Atakur, a victory stone is raised. In the words later read by scholars, it celebrates Krishna III and credits the Western Ganga prince Butuga with felling the Chola heir at Takkolam.

i18n.hi: आतकूर के पास विजय-शिला उठती है। विद्वानों की पढ़ाई में इसके शब्द कृष्ण तीसरे की जय गाते हैं, और तakkोलम में चोल युवराज को गिराने का श्रेय पश्चिमी गंग राजकुमार बुतुगा को देते हैं।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a Chola scribe in a palm-leaf-lit chamber, etching on copper plates
panels.action: In a dim Chola record room, a scribe presses his stylus into gleaming copper plates, priests and officials behind him as he incises the name of Rajaditya and the memory of his elephant death.

dialogue.text: Decades later, Chola copper plates at Tiruvalangadu and Leiden speak of Rajaditya, the prince who died upon an elephant at Takkolam, but they do not name his killer.

i18n.hi: दशक बीतते हैं। तिरुवालंगाडु और लीडन के चोल ताम्रपट राजादित्य का जिक्र करते हैं, वह राजकुमार जो तakkोलम में हाथी पर मरा, पर उसके घातक का नाम नहीं लेते।

panels.shot: split-panel feel, with faint ghosted overlays of the Atakur inscription and Chola copper plates facing each other
panels.action: Faint images of a stone inscription and copper plates appear opposite, their scripts contrasting, while behind them the ghostly outline of an elephant warrior hovers, neither side fully claiming his last moment.

dialogue.text: Here the story divides. Rashtrakuta memory is precise: Butuga’s arrow. Chola memory is proud but silent on the archer. Historians today weigh stone against copper, victory against grief.

i18n.hi: यहीं कहानी दो राहें हो जाती है। राष्ट्रकूट याद बिलकुल साफ: बुतुगा का तीर। चोल याद गर्वीली पर धुन्‍धली, धनुर्धर पर चुप। आज इतिहासकार पत्थर को ताम्र से, विजय को शोक से तौलते हैं।

panels.shot: wide, regal shot of Krishna III presiding in court, courtiers arrayed, with a map mural behind hinting at his expanded realm
panels.action: Krishna III sits firmly on a high-backed throne, courtiers at his feet and a mural behind him marking the Deccan and the south, his bearing calm, the atmosphere one of hard-won dominance.

dialogue.text: Krishna III uses his win. For a generation, Rashtrakuta influence presses deep into the south, and the Cholas live in the shadow of Takkolam’s memory before their later king Rajaraja rises to restore their glory.

i18n.hi: कृष्ण तीसरा अपनी जीत भुनाता है। एक पीढ़ी भर राष्ट्रकूट दबदबा दक्षिण तक धँसता है, और चोल तakkोलम की याद की छाया में जीते हैं, जब तक बाद में राजा राजराज उनकी शान फिर से न जगा दे।

panels.shot: quiet shot of a later Chola king, evoking Rajaraja, gazing at an inscription mentioning Rajaditya, torches flickering
panels.action: A later Chola monarch, reminiscent of Rajaraja, stands in a lamplit hall reading an inscription that recalls Rajaditya, his face a blend of pride and solemn reflection as a priest holds a torch nearby.

dialogue.text: When Rajaraja and Rajendra revive Chola power, they do not erase Takkolam. Their grants remember Rajaditya, binding their resurgence to a past defeat and a prince who fell in the north.

i18n.hi: जब राजराज और राजेंद्र चोल ताकत वापस उठाते हैं, वे तakkोलम नहीं मिटाते। उनके दान-लेख राजादित्य को याद रखते हैं, अपनी नई चढ़ाई को पुरानी हार और उत्तर में गिरे राजकुमार से बाँधते हैं।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of the Takkolam landscape today, calm fields and a distant village under soft light
panels.action: The fields around present-day Takkolam lie peaceful, with crops swaying and a village temple tower in the distance, the land giving no hint of the armies that once strained across it.

dialogue.text: We may never know whose arrow felled the prince on the elephant, but in the debate between stone and copper we see how even in certain defeat, men still compete for the last word on glory.

i18n.hi: हम शायद कभी न जानें कि किस तीर ने हाथी पर बैठे राजकुमार को गिराया, पर पत्थर और ताम्र की इस बहस में दिखता है कि पक्की हार में भी लोग आखिरी यश–कथा पर झगड़ते रहते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: At Takkolam, a prince falls, an empire buckles, and a single arrow divides memory
subtitle_i18n.hi: तक्कोलम में, एक राजकुमार गिरा, साम्राज्य डगमगाया, और एक तीर ने यादें बाँट दीं
